name: Gore S.A.M. implant

lead: Gore S.A.M. is a soft sheet or strand of expanded PTFE (ePTFE), the porous material also used in Gore-Tex fabrics, designed to be placed under the skin. In the looksmaxxing context it is discussed as a way to add volume or define facial areas without using the body's own tissue.
ePTFE is used in facial plastic surgery and in vascular and hernia repair. Its use as a facial filler has little coverage in controlled studies.

paras: A surgeon places the material through a small incision under the skin in the target area, shaping it to the contour wanted. It is a permanent surgical implant, so it is not a routine home or injectable product.

As with other implants, reported problems include infection, shifting and visible contour changes, and removal can be needed. Anyone considering it would discuss these with a qualified plastic surgeon.

angle.text: The implant adds soft-tissue bulk at the spot where it is placed, which changes the contour of that feature.

lead: Gore S.A.M. (Subcutaneous Augmentation Material) is a product made from expanded polytetrafluoroethylene, or ePTFE, the micro-porous material sold under the Gore-Tex name [1]. It belongs to the family of ePTFE facial implants used to build up or reshape soft tissue areas.

Wikipedia lists facial plastic surgery among the uses of ePTFE implants, alongside cardiac and vascular reconstruction and hernia repair [1]. In ascension forums the material is discussed alongside other implants for lips, cheeks and the nose.

paras: ePTFE is a porous form of PTFE used as a graft material and implant in surgery, including facial plastic surgery [1]. S.A.M. is a Gore product made of this material for soft-tissue augmentation.

PTFE itself is chemically stable, with deterioration only at temperatures around 260 C and above [1]. Surgical complications and removal rates for facial use are matters for the surgeon and the procedure-specific literature.
